stem:
Ishan bubbles his exhaled air through lime water in one tube. Fresh air from outside is bubbled through lime water in a second tube. Only the exhaled-air tube turns milky. Both tubes start with clear lime water.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Exhaled air has more carbon dioxide than the fresh air he tested.
Exhaled air still contains some oxygen.
Lime water turning milky proves that oxygen increased in the exhaled-air tube.
Exhaled air contains no oxygen at all.

teacher.key_rationale: Milky lime water shows more carbon dioxide in exhaled air than in the fresh-air tube. Exhaled air still contains oxygen; it is not oxygen-free, and milky lime water does not mean oxygen rose.
